flags: TaskUs's Board of Directors declared a special cash dividend of $3.65 per share, totaling $332.8 million, on February 25, 2026, which was paid on March 25, 2026 and recorded as (332,788) (table in thousands) in dividend distributions.

On March 11, 2026, TaskUs entered into the 2026 Credit Agreement, including a $500.0 million term loan facility and a $100.0 million revolving credit facility, to repay prior credit facility borrowings, pay fees, and fund the special dividend, with long-term debt rising from 219,798 to 462,897 (table in thousands).

In conjunction with the Special Dividend, TaskUs made proportionate adjustments to outstanding equity awards under its incentive plans, resulting in $1.2 million of stock-based compensation expense and a $6.7 million reclassification from additional paid-in capital to accrued payroll and employee-related liabilities.

business_model.claim: TaskUs delivers outsourced digital services across Digital Customer Experience, Trust & Safety, and Artificial Intelligence Services.
quotes: Our global, omnichannel delivery model is focused on providing our clients with three key services – Digital Customer Experience (“Digital CX”), Trust & Safety and Artificial Intelligence (“AI”) Services.

business_model.claim: In 2025, Digital Customer Experience, Trust & Safety, and Artificial Intelligence Services represented 56%, 26%, and 18% of TaskUs's $1,183.5 million total service revenue.
quotes: For the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025, Digital Customer Experience, Trust & Safety and Artificial Intelligence Services represented 56%, 26% and 18%, respectively, of our total service revenue of $1,183.5 million compared to 61%, 25% and 14%, respectively, of our total service revenue of $995.0 million for the year ended December 31, 2024.

business_model.claim: Digital Customer Experience primarily delivers omnichannel customer care through lower-cost non-voice digital channels alongside learning experience and sales and customer acquisition services.
quotes: Our digitally native service offerings enable us to utilize lower-cost non-voice channels.
We leverage chat, social, in-app support, SMS, and in-platform solutions and apply an “automation first” mentality to our client engagements.
Also included in this offering are learning experience and sales and customer acquisition services.

business_model.claim: Trust & Safety provides content moderation for online platforms as well as financial crime and compliance services including identity verification, regulatory compliance, and fraud detection.
quotes: Trust & Safety consists of two primary areas of service: Content Moderation and Financial Crime & Compliance.

Content Moderation pertains to the process of monitoring, reviewing and managing user and advertiser-generated content on online platforms to ensure it complies with community guidelines, legal regulations, and platform-specific policies.
Financial Crime & Compliance pertains to services designed to protect end users, detect and eliminate fraud, address unwanted user activity, and manage regulatory compliance.

business_model.claim: Artificial Intelligence Services supports clients across the machine learning lifecycle through large language model support, data collection and annotation, AI safety, and real-world AI deployment management.
quotes: Our teams support key stages across our customers’ machine learning lifecycle: pre-training data collection and preparation, post-training evaluation, and continuous model assessment.
Through our relationship with autonomous vehicle and robotics companies we have built capabilities in deploying and managing the performance of AI in real-world production environments.

business_model.claim: TaskUs bills clients on time-and-materials, cost-plus, unit-priced, fixed-price, or outcome-oriented bases as services are delivered.
quotes: As these services are delivered, we bill our clients on either time-and-materials, cost-plus, unit-priced, fixed-price, or outcome oriented basis.

business_model.claim: TaskUs serves approximately 200 clients across industries including AI, autonomous vehicles, robotics, social media, financial services, and healthcare, generating over $1.0 million in 2025 revenue from 98 clients.
quotes: By combining specialized human talent and intelligent technology, we solve complex operational challenges for global category leaders within AI, autonomous vehicles, robotics, social media, financial services, healthcare, and beyond.
As of December 31, 2025, we supported approximately 200 of the world’s leading companies and generated revenue in excess of $1.0 million from 98 of these clients during 2025.

business_model.claim: Revenue is concentrated among large clients: in 2025, the top client accounted for 26% of revenue, the top five 45%, the top ten 58%, and the top twenty 71%.
quotes: Our top client accounted for an aggregate of 26% of our revenue for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025, across multiple service offerings.
Our top five clients accounted for 45% of our revenue for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025.

business_model.claim: Client engagements are typically non-exclusive without long-term volume commitments and often permit termination for convenience with advance notice.
quotes: However, the volume of work performed for any specific client is likely to vary from year to year, especially since we generally are not our clients’ exclusive outsourcing provider and we generally do not have long-term commitments from clients to purchase our services and solutions.

Our contracts are typically one to three years in length with automatic renewal provisions, but certain contracts may provide for termination for cause under certain circumstances or at the client’s convenience with advance notice and may or may not include penalties or required payments in the event the termination right is exercised.

business_model.claim: TaskUs operates an offshore and nearshore delivery footprint of approximately 65,500 employees across 31 sites in 13 countries, with 87% of 2025 revenue delivered via non-voice digital or omnichannel services.
quotes: As of December 31, 2025, our worldwide Headcount totaled approximately 65,500 people across 31 sites in 13 countries capable of delivering services in more than 30 languages.

87% of our revenue for the year ended December 31, 2025 was delivered from non-voice, digital channels or omnichannel services which allow us to utilize resources efficiently, thereby driving higher profitability.

business_model.claim: In 2025, service delivery originated in the Philippines ($638,042, table in thousands), Rest of World ($259,681, table in thousands), India ($153,766, table in thousands), and the United States ($132,058, table in thousands), while most contracts require payment in U.S. dollars.
quotes: We deliver our services from multiple locations around the world; however, the majority of our service revenues are derived from contracts that require payment in United States dollars, regardless of whether the clients are located in the United States.

business_model.claim: Revenue growth is driven by existing-client expansion—with a 113% net revenue retention rate, 67 clients signing new statements of work, and 73 clients using multiple service lines in 2025—alongside 34 new client wins at a 36% win rate.
quotes: We won 34 new clients in 2025, and we achieved a 36% new client win rate for every dollar of new client opportunities we pursued.
In 2025, 67 current clients signed new statements of work with us.

We also made progress on our strategic goal of cross-selling our suite of specialized services to our client base, increasing the number of clients using more than one service line by 14% year-over-year to 73 clients.

quotes: In some cases, TaskUs is supporting these initiatives, which may lead to revenue growth in the near term but may ultimately result in the automation of some services that TaskUs currently provides for these clients.

business_model.claim: Cost of services is TaskUs's largest expense—$736,361 (table in thousands) in 2025 and $205,883 (table in thousands, up 11.0%) in the third quarter of 2026—driven primarily by frontline personnel, site, and delivery technology costs.
quotes: Cost of services consists primarily of costs related to delivery of services, and consists primarily of personnel costs like salaries and wages, stock-based compensation expense and employee welfare.
The increase was primarily driven by higher personnel costs of $108.2 million associated with increased headcount and facilities costs associated with site expansion.

business_model.claim: In the third quarter of 2026, higher headcount, an operating shift to higher-cost geographies—as United States delivery revenue rose 74.7%—and expansion into autonomous-vehicle field services drove $13.3 million in additional personnel costs alongside higher facilities rent and software expenses.
quotes: The increase was primarily driven by higher personnel costs of $13.3 million associated with increased headcount and the operating shift to higher cost geographies.
The remaining increase included costs associated with our expansion into field services for developers of autonomous vehicles, facilities rent and related fees and software.

business_model.claim: Labor costs and margins depend on annual wage increases, employee attrition—which was 26.6% in 2025 for employees with more than 180 days of tenure—and managing unassigned headcount when contracts end.
quotes: Apart from driving our high client satisfaction and retention metrics, lower employee attrition leads to lower hiring and training costs and higher employee productivity.
The voluntary attrition rate for employees who were employed by TaskUs for more than 180 days was 26.6% for the year ended December 31, 2025.

Termination or non-renewal of a client contract could cause us to experience a higher than expected number of unassigned employees and thus compress our margins until we are able to reallocate our headcount.

business_model.basis: stated in F2, P3, and P4
business_model.claim: Selling, general and administrative expenses totaled $244,888 (table in thousands) in 2025 and fell (8.1)% year-over-year to $54,850 (table in thousands) in the third quarter of 2026, driven by sales, marketing, and corporate overhead plus fluctuating stock-based compensation, transaction, litigation, and operational efficiency costs.
quotes: General and administrative expenses consist of personnel costs and related expenses for technology, human resources, legal, finance, global shared services, and executives as well as professional fees, insurance premiums, cloud-based capabilities and other corporate expenses.

The decrease was primarily driven by lower personnel costs of $2.8 million, due to a $2.1 million reduction in stock-based compensation expense, as well as lower transaction costs of $1.8 million and lower operational efficiency costs of $0.9 million.

business_model.basis: stated in F2, P3, and P4
business_model.claim: Costs and below-the-line results are also affected by site-and-hardware depreciation ($12,318, table in thousands, in the third quarter of 2026), foreign currency movements and hedges, and financing expenses, which rose 93.0% to $8,929 (table in thousands) in the third quarter of 2026 after the 2026 debt refinancing.
quotes: The increase was primarily driven by site expansions and the acquisition of technology hardware to support increased headcount.

Fluctuations in foreign currencies impact the amount of total assets, liabilities, revenue, operating expenses and cash flows that we report for our foreign subsidiaries upon the translation of these amounts into U.S. Dollars.
The increase was primarily driven by a higher outstanding principal balance and interest rate following the Refinancing.

competitive_position.claim: TaskUs's content moderation business faces workforce mental-health legal claims, negative publicity, recruiting and retention challenges, and regulatory uncertainty including potential changes to CDA Section 230.
